stem:
Meena wants to light a small torch bulb using one dry cell. She tries four different arrangements of connecting wires between the cell and the bulb.
In which arrangement will the bulb glow?

options.text: One wire joins the positive terminal of the cell to one side of the bulb, and the other side of the bulb is left unconnected.
One wire joins the positive terminal of the cell to one side of the bulb, and a second wire joins the other side of the bulb to the negative terminal of the cell.
One wire joins both terminals of the cell together, and the bulb is held near the cell without touching it.
Two wires join the positive terminal of the cell to both sides of the bulb, and the negative terminal is left unconnected.

teacher.key_rationale: The bulb glows only when there is a complete conducting path: one terminal of the cell connected to one terminal (side) of the bulb and the other terminal of the cell to the other side of the bulb. Only arrangement B provides this complete circuit; A and D leave one terminal unconnected, and C makes no contact with the bulb at all.
